_comment: IMPORTANT - the folder on the stick MUST be named SMEG_PLUS_UPG for the user_data half of this scheme to apply. C_UPGRADE::UpgradeTask calls IsDirExist('/bd0/SMEG_PLUS_UPG/NAV/USER_DATA') and only then does 'Copy of /USERDATA from /bd0 to NAND'; both the folder name and the module are literal in that string. This scheme writes to SMEG_PLUS_UPG_auxdefault so it does not clobber a stock copy, so RENAME IT when you put it on the stick. If you do not, the copy is skipped silently, the rest of the update succeeds, and the unit still boots to whatever it booted to before - which is indistinguishable from the setting being wrong. Source enum recovered from the per-source OnEventSelect* handlers in C_HMI_AUDIO_APP_BASE (the value each passes to CreateNotificationCommand): FM=1 AM=2 DAB=3 BT=5 CDC=6 AUX=7 iPod=10 Juke=11. 4 is not a valid source, which is why the first attempt fell back to FM. Force AUX as the default source. Two halves: (1) `media.settings` edits the seed database inside system.bin, and (2) `user_data` ships that database as the NAV/USER_DATA payload, because that is where the unit actually reads its live settings - system.bin extracts to the read-only /SYSTEM/, so editing it alone changes nothing (confirmed on the car: still booted to FM). user_data ships ONLY up_common.sqlite, deliberately, so the unit's other personal state is left as alone as this mechanism allows. LOCAL build manifest - the paths below are absolute for one checkout, so edit them before reusing. Force AUX as the default source. Step 1 of the plan in issue #72: a DATA edit only, so there is no code patch and nothing can be bricked. `supervisor.Last_Source` is the value C_MGR_SRC::StartUp() restores at boot (saved by C_MGR_SRC::ImmediateSourceSave()). AUX is position 4 per the 0-based source list in C_HMI_AUDIO_APP_BASE::GetSourceAtPosition(). If the unit ignores it, try varying supervisor.Last_Source_Priority (currently 1) alongside it. If 4 lands on the WRONG source, the position guess is wrong - report what it did land on and it can be corrected from a single flash rather than a guess.
